text:
## Recommended approach: **Offline-first, mobile data collection + cloud database + simple admin dashboard**

For your context, I would **not** start with a full custom software build or a generic “all-in-one” ERP.  
The best fit is a **low-code, offline-capable field reporting system** using:

- **KoBoToolbox** or **ODK Collect** for field data capture
- **Airtable** or **Google Sheets** only for very simple back-office tracking
- **Power BI / Looker Studio** for reporting, if needed
- **Android phones/tablets** dedicated to field staff
- A lightweight training and support package

Because the staff have **low digital literacy**, the system should be built around:
- short forms
- dropdowns instead of free text
- photo capture where useful
- offline sync when connectivity is available
- minimal typing
- one simple workflow at a time

---

# Best specific option: **KoBoToolbox + Android devices**

KoBoToolbox is a strong fit because it is:
- designed for low-connectivity settings
- free for many nonprofit use cases
- good for forms, surveys, case intake, visits, referrals, and basic follow-up
- usable offline through Android phones with **KoBoCollect**

If your nonprofit mainly needs to digitize:
- beneficiary registration
- household visits
- service delivery logs
- referrals
- case notes
- simple monitoring reports

then this is the most practical and affordable route.

---

# Proposed system

## Tools
1. **KoBoToolbox**  
   - form creation
   - offline field data collection
   - syncing when internet becomes available

2. **KoBoCollect app** on Android devices  
   - used by field staff

3. **A shared laptop/desktop** for the admin team  
   - to review submissions and export to Excel/CSV

4. **Optional: Looker Studio or Excel**  
   - simple dashboards and reporting

---

# Budget estimate under PHP 400,000

Below is a realistic implementation budget.

## 1) Devices for field staff
Assume 10 field staff need devices, not all 30 staff.

- **10 Android smartphones/tablets** @ PHP 12,000 each = **PHP 120,000**

Reasonable mid-range Android devices are enough for forms and photos.

## 2) Protective accessories and power support
- Cases, screen protectors, power banks, charging cables = **PHP 25,000**

This matters because field conditions are rough and electricity is intermittent.

## 3) Setup and configuration
- Form design, workflow setup, user roles, initial database structure = **PHP 50,000**

This includes converting paper forms into digital forms and testing them.

## 4) Staff training
- 2 training sessions + job aids in Filipino/English + hands-on coaching = **PHP 45,000**

Low digital literacy means training is essential.

## 5) Data cleanup and migration
- Encode key legacy paper records, if needed = **PHP 40,000**

Do not try to digitize every old paper file. Prioritize:
- active clients
- current cases
- last 12–24 months of important records

## 6) Internet/data and support for 18 months
- Load/stipend for syncing and admin use = **PHP 36,000**  
  (about PHP 2,000/month for admin connectivity and syncing support)

## 7) Technical support / maintenance
- part-time local IT/helpdesk support = **PHP 50,000**

## 8) Contingency
- unexpected costs = **PHP 34,000**

---

## Total
**PHP 400,000**

### Breakdown
- Devices: PHP 120,000
- Accessories: PHP 25,000
- Setup/configuration: PHP 50,000
- Training: PHP 45,000
- Data migration: PHP 40,000
- Connectivity for 18 months: PHP 36,000
- Technical support: PHP 50,000
- Contingency: PHP 34,000

**Grand total: PHP 400,000**

---

# Why this is the right approach

## Fits offline conditions
Field staff can collect data without internet and sync later.

## Low learning curve
KoBo forms are simpler than many business systems.

## Low recurring cost
KoBoToolbox itself can be used at low or no license cost depending on account scale and use case.

## Fast deployment
You can launch in weeks, not months.

## Easier to sustain
The nonprofit can maintain basic operations after donor funding ends without paying for expensive licenses.

---

# What I would avoid

## Avoid a custom-built system
A custom app would likely exceed the budget and create dependency on a developer.

## Avoid a full enterprise platform
Systems like Salesforce, Dynamics, or full ERP products will be too expensive and too complex for 30 staff with low digital literacy.

## Avoid paper-to-digital “big bang” conversion
Do not digitize everything at once. Start with core workflows only.

---

# What happens when donor funding ends in 18 months?

The system should be designed to **keep working with minimal ongoing cost**.

## At month 18, the system continues as follows:
- Field staff keep using the same Android devices
- Forms remain in KoBoToolbox
- Data continues to sync when internet is available
- Admin staff continue exporting reports to Excel/CSV
- The nonprofit uses the system with very low monthly cost

## Ongoing costs after donor funding
Likely recurring expenses:
- mobile data/load
- occasional device replacement
- part-time admin or IT support
- backup storage and reporting time

Estimated post-donor operating cost:
- **PHP 3,000–8,000/month**, depending on number of users and device replacement needs

That means the nonprofit should be able to sustain the system if it builds a small operating budget into general expenses or fundraising.

---

# Sustainability plan after 18 months

To avoid collapse after donor funding ends:

## 1) Keep the tech stack simple
Use KoBoToolbox + Android devices + Excel/Google Sheets exports.

## 2) Assign internal owners
At least 2 staff should be trained as “super users” who can:
- edit forms
- onboard staff
- troubleshoot basic issues

## 3) Budget for replacement and data
Add a small annual IT line item:
- device replacement
- load/data
- support

## 4) Use standard formats
Keep exports in CSV/Excel so data is not trapped in one vendor.

## 5) Document workflows
Create:
- one-page SOPs
- field guide
- naming conventions
- data entry rules

---

# If you want a slightly more powerful option
If the nonprofit needs **case management**, not just forms, then consider:

- **CommCare** for case tracking and longitudinal client management

CommCare is excellent for NGOs and offline use, but it may cost more than KoBo depending on scale and plan. With your budget, KoBo is usually the safer choice unless you need strong case-management logic.

---

# Final recommendation
**Use KoBoToolbox + KoBoCollect on Android devices, with a simple admin dashboard in Excel/Looker Studio.**  
This gives you an offline-first system, fits low digital literacy, and stays within **PHP 400,000**.

### Total cost: **PHP 400,000**
### Status after donor funding ends:
The system **continues operating** with only modest recurring costs for data, support, and device maintenance. It should not require new donor funding to keep functioning, provided the nonprofit maintains a small annual IT budget and trains internal super users.

If you want, I can also give you:
1. a **30/60/90-day implementation plan**, or  
2. a **more detailed budget with line-item procurement specs** for the Philippines.
